summary_paragraph: A 59-year-old woman with advanced HIV and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted for a right femoral dialysis catheter infection, presenting with leg pain, swelling, and purulent drainage. She was hypotensive on arrival but stabilized with fluids. The infected catheter was removed, and she received a 7-day course of vancomycin. A new tunneled catheter was successfully placed on the left side after an initial failed attempt. Imaging initially suggested a possible IVC thrombus, prompting a brief course of heparin, but a subsequent CT confirmed no clot, and anticoagulation was discontinued. She remained afebrile and blood cultures were negative. During admission, she was treated for presumed oral candidiasis, and her aspirin dose was increased due to a history of atrial fibrillation. Medication adjustments included reducing sevelamer, starting Nephrocaps, and modifying HIV prophylaxis. She improved clinically and was discharged home with follow-up planned in nephrology, infectious disease, and social work.
